title: On boundary layers and upstream influence. I. A comparison between subsonic and supersonic flows
author_display: Michael James Lighthill and Maxwell Herman Alexander Newman
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences
abstract_orig: It is pointed out that there are two separate mechanisms for upstream influence through the boundary layer in supersonic flow, and that one of these (that involving separation) operates also in subsonic flow. A quantitative theory of subsonic flow up a step is given to illustrate this. The main differences between the subsonic and supersonic flows are as follows: (i) The boundaries of dead-air regions are nearly straight in supersonic flow but are usually highly curved in subsonic flow. (ii) Separation (whether of the laminar or turbulent layer) occurs at a much lower pressure coefficient in supersonic flow; this is only slightly due to the fact that the fluid nearest the wall is then lighter and so more easily brought to rest; it is due much more to the relative suddenness of the pressure rise ahead of the dead-air region. (iii) However, for a given pressure coefficient in the dead-air region, the distance of upstream influence is somewhat greater in the subsonic flow, except at the highest pressures. A qualitative discussion of the second mechanism of upstream influence, in supersonic flow, is given; for a quantitative theory of this see part II (Lighthill 1953).

title: An experimental investigation of the interaction between shock waves and boundary layers
author_display: G. E. Gadd, Douglas William Holder and J. D. Regan
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences
abstract_orig: Abstract An account is given of an investigation into the interaction between the boundary layer on a flat plate and a shock wave produced either externally, by a wedge in the supersonic mainstream, or from within the boundary layer, by a wedge held in contact with the plate. A wide range of free-stream Mach numbers, boundary-layer Reynolds numbers, and shock strengths has been covered, shock strength being defined as the ratio of the static pressure downstream of the shock to the static pressure upstream of it. Variations in these parameters can have large effects on the interaction, and there are also large differences between cases with externally generated shocks and cases where the shock is generated from within the boundary layer. The investigation has thrown light on the physical mechanisms involved. It is found that many of the major features of the interaction arise because the boundary layer separates from the surface ahead of the shock wave.The conditions under which separation occurs and the behaviour of the separated boundary layer thus have important effects, in terms of which, for example, the differences between the interactions observed with laminar and with turbulent boundary layers may be explained.

title: Experimental Investigation of the Pressure Rise Required for the Incipient Separation of Turbulent Boundary Layers in Two-Dimensional Supersonic Flow
abstract_orig: An experimental investigation has been made of turbulent boundary-layer separation associated with compression corners, curved surfaces of various radii, and incident shock waves. The purpose of the investigation was to provide design information, and to define significant physical trends, which would aid in the prediction of turbulent separation for various aerodynamic devices, such as compressor blades, flaps, spoilers, and diffusers. A characteristic change in the longitudinal static-pressure distribution (i.e., a change from a curve with one inflection point to a curve with three inflection points) was employed to detect the occurrence of separation. The effects of Reynolds number (10(exp 6) to 10(exp 7) per foot or l.5 x 10(exp 4) to 7.5 x 10(exp 4) based upon boundary-layer thickness) and Mach number (1.6 to 4.2) on the onset of turbulent boundary-layer separation were investigated. The pressure gradient of the boundary-layer flow ahead of the interaction region was essentially zero. The results show a considerable effect of Mach number on the pressure rise for incipient separation for all configurations. For a curved-surface model, the static pressure-rise ratio required to cause separation varied from about 2.5, at a Mach number of 2 to about 16, at a Mach number of 3.5. A substantial effect of Reynolds number on the pressure rise for incipient separation was observed in the upper Mach number range and in the lower Reynolds number range; namely, the pressure rise required for separation decreased with increasing Reynolds number. For low Mach numbers and high Reynolds numbers, there appeared to be no Reynolds number effect. The effects of Mach number and of Reynolds number were similar for all models. Model shape was also found to be an important variable affecting the onset of separation. Large gains were realized in the pressure-rise ratio with no separation when the radius of curvature of the model surface was increased. At a Mach number of 3.4, for instance, the pressure-rise ratio with no separation increased from about 5 to 15 as a result of an increase in the radius of curvature from approximately 0 to 30 boundary-layer thicknesses.

title: Self-induced separation
author_display: Keith Stewartson and P. G. Williams
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences
abstract_orig: A rational theory is developed to explain the initial pressure rise and consequent separation of a laminar boundary layer when it interacts with a moderately strong shock. In this theory, which is firmly based on the linearized theory of Lighthill (1953), the region of interest is divided into three parts: the major part of the boundary layer, which is shown to change under largely inviscid forces, the supersonic main stream just adjacent to the boundary layer in which the pressure variation is small; and a region close to the wall, on boundary-layer scale, in which the relative variation of the velocity is large but is controlled by the incompressible boundary-layer equations, together with novel boundary conditions. We find that the first two parts can be handled in a straightforward way and the problem of self-induced separation reduces, in its essentials, to the solution of a single problem in the theory of incompressible boundary layers. It is found that this problem has three solutions, one of which corresponds to undisturbed flow and another describes a boundary layer which, spontaneously, generates an adverse pressure gradient and a decreasing skin friction which eventually vanishes and then downstream a reversed flow is set up. The third solution generates a favourable pressure gradient and is not relevant to the present study. Although there has hitherto been no valid numerical method of integrating a boundary layer with reversed flow, we find that an ad hoc method seems to lead to a stable solution which has a number of the properties to be expected of a separated boundary layer. Comparison with experiment gives qualitatively good agreement, but quantitatively errors of the order of 20% are found. It is believed that these errors arise because the Reynolds numbers at which the experiments were carried out are too small.

title: On the lengthscales of laminar shock/boundary-layer interaction
abstract_orig: The interaction of an oblique shock with a laminar boundary layer on an adiabatic flat plate is analysed by solving the Navier-Stokes equations numerically. Mach numbers range from 1.4 to 3.4 and Reynolds numbers range from 10 5 to 6 × 10 5. The numerical results agree well with experiments. The pressure distribution at the edge of the boundary layer is proposed as a sensitive indicator of the numerical resolution. Local and global properties of the interaction region are discussed. In the vicinity of the separation point, local scaling laws of the free interaction are confirmed. For the length of the separation bubble a new similarity law reveals a linear influence of the shock strength. A comparison with the triple-deck theory shows that, for finite Reynolds numbers, the triple deck tends to overestimate the lengthscale substantially and that this discrepancy increases with increasing Mach number. The triple-deck model of displacing the main part of the boundary layer is substantiated by the numerical results. An asymmetrical structure within the separation bubble causes a characteristic distribution of the wall shear stress.

title: The effect of the upstream boundary-layer state on the shock interaction at a compression corner
author_display: Kiyotaka Hayakawa and L. C. Squire
abstract_orig: In most experimental studies of the shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction at a compression corner the boundary layer upstream of the interaction has developed in zero-pressure-gradient conditions. However, in many practical situations the boundary layer upstream of the interaction is subject to adverse or favourable pressure gradients, and hence is in a non-equilibrium state. This paper presents the results of a series of experiments on the interaction at a compression corner where the boundary layer upstream of the corner is disturbed by air injected through a porous surface. The results are thus of direct interest to the design of transpiration-cooled aerodynamic surfaces. However, the boundary-layer profiles upstream of the interaction also have many similarities to those in an adverse pressure gradient, so that the results also give some indication of the effects of an isentropic compression upstream of the interaction. title: Separation length in high-enthalpy shock/boundary-layer interaction
abstract_orig: Experiments were performed in the T5 Hypervelocity Shock Tunnel to investigate nonequilibrium real-gas effects on separation length using a double-wedge geometry and nitrogen test gas. Local external flow conditions were estimated by computing the inviscid nonequilibrium flow field. A new scaling parameter was developed to approximately account for wall temperature effects on separation length for a laminar nonreacting boundary layer and arbitrary viscosity law. A classification was introduced to divide mechanisms for real-gas effects into those acting internal and external to viscous regions of the flow. Internal mechanisms were further subdivided into those arising upstream and downstream of separation. Analysis based on the ideal dissociating gas model and a scaling law for separation length of a nonreacting boundary layer showed that external mechanisms due to dissociation may decrease separation length at low incidence but depend on the free-stream dissociation at high incidence. A limited numerical study of reacting boundary layers showed that internal mechanisms due to recombination occurring in the boundary layer upstream of separation cause a slight decrease in separation length relative to a nonreacting boundary layer with the same external conditions. Correlations were obtained of experimentally measured separation length using local external flow parameters computed for reacting flow, which scales out external mechanisms but not internal mechanisms. These showed the importance of the new scaling parameter in high-enthalpy flows, a linear relationship between separation length and reattachment pressure ratio, and a Reynolds-number effect for transitional interactions. A significant increase in scaled separation length was observed in the experimental data at high enthalpy. The increase was attributed to an internal mechanism arising from recombination in the free-shear layer downstream of separation, perhaps altering its velocity profile. This real-gas effect depends on the combined presence of free-stream dissociation and a cold wall.

title: Laminar boundary-layer separation control by Görtler-scale blowing
author_display: L. L. van Dommelen and R. Yapalparvi
abstract_orig: Recent experimental work has succeeded in retarding or removing boundary-layer separation by means of blowing supersonic microjets transversely through the wall. To provide some theoretical context for such work, the current study examines the removal of separation by transverse blowing within the framework of the standard Prandtl scalings for incompressible boundary layers. One key result, obtained using asymptotic analysis, is that such removal is not possible for two-dimensional flow. Neither is removal of separation possible by three-dimensional blowing in an initially two-dimensional separated boundary layer if the blowing distribution has a finite-scale spanwise variation. The second key result obtained is that the previous conclusion is no longer valid when there is nontrivial short-scale spanwise variation of the blowing distribution. This result is obtained by providing a numerical counter-example in which blowing, with a Görtler scale spanwise variation, creates an attached boundary layer flow where none existed before the blowing. One consequence is that there are at least some flows in which transverse Görtler-scale blowing can turn a separated flow into an attached flow, with a vanishingly small drag that is inversely proportional to the square root of the Reynolds number. The flow physics of the computed example is analyzed to obtain a better understanding of how the Görtler-scale blowing affects the flow.

abstract_orig:
The first contribution of this paper is the extension of the
non-iterative transformation method, proposed by T\”opfer
more than a century ago and defined for the numerical solution of the

This method, which makes use of the invariance of two physical
parameters with respect to an extended scaling group of point

method is an initial value method. However, in this way, we cannot fix

compute the numerical solution for given values of the two parameters we
have to define an iterative extension of the transformation method,

title: Hypersonic shock impingement studies on a flat plate: flow separation of laminar boundary layers
author_display: Eric Won Keun Chang et al.
abstract_orig: Interactions between shock waves and boundary layers produce flow separations and augmented pressure/thermal loads in hypersonic flight. This study provides details of Mach 7 impinging-shock-flat-plate experiments conducted in the T4 Stalker Tube. Measurements were taken at flow conditions of Mach 7.0 (2.44 MJ kg ⁻¹) and Mach 7.7 (2.88 MJ kg ⁻¹) flight enthalpies with a range of freestream unit Reynolds numbers from 1.43 × 10⁶ m ⁻¹ to 5.01 × 10⁶ m ⁻¹. A shock generator at 12^{° } or 16^{° } to the freestream created an oblique shock which impinged on a boundary layer over a flat plate to induce flow separation. The flow field was examined using simultaneous measurements of wall static pressure, heat transfer and schlieren visualisation. Measured heat transfer along the flat plate without the shock impingement indicated that the boundary layer remained laminar for all flow conditions. The shock impingement flow field was successfully established within the facility test duration. The onset of separation was observed by a rise in wall pressure and a decrease in heat transfer at the location corresponding to the stem of the separation shock. Downstream of this initial rise, an increased pressure and higher heating loads were observed. The heat-transfer levels also indicated an immediate boundary layer transition due to the shock impingement. The separation data of the present work showed good agreement with our previous work on shock impingement on heated walls (Chang et al., J. Fluid Mech., vol. 908, 2021, pp. 1–13). A comparison with the previous scaling indicated that the separation also relates to the pressure ratio and the wall temperature parameter.

title: Instabilities in oblique shock wave/laminar boundary-layer interactions
author_display: F. Guiho, F. Alizard and J.-Ch. Robinet
abstract_orig: The interaction of an oblique shock wave and a laminar boundary layer developing over a ﬂat plate is investigated by means of numerical simulation and global linear-stability analysis. Under the selected ﬂow conditions (free-stream Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers and shock-wave angles), the incoming boundary layer undergoes separation due to the adverse pressure gradient. For a wide range of ﬂow parameters, the oblique shock wave/boundary-layer interaction (OSWBLI) is seen to be globally stable. We show that the onset of two-dimensional large-scale structures is generated by selective noise ampliﬁcation that is described for each frequency, in a linear framework, by wave-packet trains composed of several global modes. A detailed analysis of both the eigenspectrum and eigenfunctions gives some insight into the relationship between spatial scales (shape and localization) and frequencies. In particular, OSWBLI exhibits a universal behaviour. The lowest frequencies correspond to structures mainly located near the separated shock that emit radiation in the form of Mach waves and are scaled by the interaction length. The medium frequencies are associated with structures mainly localized in the shear layer and are scaled by the displacement thickness at the impact. The linear process by which OSWBLI selects frequencies is analysed by means of the global resolvent. It shows that unsteadiness are mainly associated with instabilities arising from the shear layer. For the lower frequency range, there is no particular selectivity in a linear framework. Two-dimensional numerical simulations show that the linear behaviour is modiﬁed for moderate forcing amplitudes by nonlinear mechanisms leading to a signiﬁcant ampliﬁcation of low frequencies. Finally, based on the present results, we draw some hypotheses concerning the onset of unsteadiness observed in shock wave/turbulent boundary-layer interactions.

title: Global instability of the interaction between an oblique shock and a laminar boundary layer
abstract_orig: This study investigates the oblique shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction with a Mach number of 2.15 and a Reynolds number of 1 105. Both global stability analysis and direct numerical simulation are used to reveal the global instability characteristics and three-dimensional details of the incident shock flow. The results of global stability analysis indicate that stationary global instability occurs when the shock angle exceeds the critical angle 31:8. At a shock angle equal to 33, an additional unstable mode appears, which is oscillatory at large wavelength and gradually dominant when the wavelength decreases. As the wavelength is further reduced, the mode and its conjugation evolve into two stationary modes with different growth rates. A global instability criterion for incident shock flow is established based on the triple deck theory, which determines the instability only through free-stream conditions and shock angles. A direct numerical simulation is performed for the 32 shock angle case. It is found that secondary separation occurs during the nonlinear growth, which is absent in the two-dimensional base flow. Moreover, the separated flow undergoes a secondary perturbation growth, during which the dominant spanwise wavelength is doubled and the flow structures change significantly. The flow oscillates around a quasi-steady state in the end, indicating that a stationary unstable mode can develop unsteadiness without external disturbances.

abstract_orig: , The flow instabilities in shock-wave–boundary-layer interactions at Mach 6 are comprehensively investigated through compression corner and incident shock cases. title: Experimental investigation of the effects of a moving wall on the separation bubble in a hypersonic ramp–flat plate configuration
abstract_orig: Shock Wave/Boundary Layer Interaction is a fundamental problem in hypersonic flows. This study investigates the influence of a moving wall on the flow separation region in a Mach 5 hypersonic flow using high-speed schlieren imaging and high-frequency pressure measurements. The results indicate that the moving wall alters the length and height of the separation bubble and reveal that low-frequency modes dominate the flow evolution between the wedge and the plate, and high-frequency modes capture the influence of the leading-edge shock. The moving wall’s influence has three distinct stages. The interaction among the incident shock, the separation shock, and the separation bubble governs the first two stages. The third stage involves the interaction with the leading-edge shock. The differing states of the boundary layer on the moving wall led to distinct trends in the evolution of separation length and height between the first and second stages. Pressure measurements show a consistent trend of pressure fluctuation at various locations on the plate, although the duration and rate of change differ. For a fixed wedge angle, these variations in pressure response are attributed to the different states of the boundary layer on the moving wall. Finally, this paper gives a theoretical model describing the temporal evolution of the separation bubble’s length and height based on the free interaction theory and experimental data. These findings offer new insights into controlling shock boundary layer interaction in highspeed flows through a moving wall.

title: Investigation of unsteady, hypersonic, laminar separated flows over a double cone geometry using a kinetic approach
author_display: Ozgur Tumuklu, Deborah A. Levin and Vassilis Theofilis
abstract_orig: Shock-dominated hypersonic laminar flows over a double cone are investigated using time accurate direct simulation Monte Carlo combined with the residuals algorithm for unit Reynolds numbers gradually increasing from 9.35 × 104 to 3.74 × 105 m-1 at a Mach number of about 16. The main flow features, such as the strong bow-shock, location of the separation shock, the triple point, and the entire laminar separated region, show a time-dependent behavior. Although the separation shock angle is found to be similar for all Re numbers, the effects of Reynolds number on the structure and extent of the separation region are profound. As the Reynolds number is increased, larger pressure values in the under-expanded jet region due to strong shock interactions form more prominent λ-shocklets in the supersonic region between two contact surfaces. Likewise, the surface parameters, especially on the second cone surface, show a strong dependence on the Reynolds number, with skin friction, pressure, and surface heating rates increasing and velocity slip and temperature jump values decreasing for increasing Re number. A Kelvin-Helmholtz instability arising at the shear layer results in an unsteady flow for the highest Reynolds number. These findings suggest that consideration of experimental measurement times is important when it comes to determining the steady state surface parameters even for a relatively simple double cone geometry at moderately large Reynolds numbers.

title: Experimental Study on Unsteadiness in Hypersonic Shock Wave/Turbulent Boundary Layer Interaction
abstract_orig: The interaction between shock waves and thick boundary layers formed on the surface of an aircraft results in complex phenomena of shock wave/boundary layer interaction (SBLI). Local damage and rapid material fatigue on the aircraft’s surface, severely affecting aircraft safety, can be attributed to the peak heat ﬂux within the turbulent boundary layer interaction zone and the low-frequency oscillation characteristics of shock waves. In this study, the unsteady characteristics of shock waveturbulent boundary layer interactions were investigated in hypersonic wind tunnel at the China Academy of Aerospace Aerodynamics. Advanced testing methodologies, such as infrared thermographic technology, ﬂuctuation pressure measurement technology, and high-speed laser schlieren technology, were utilized to acquire data on ﬂow topology, wave system structure, surface heat ﬂux, and oscillation frequency of separation shock within the interaction zones of 34° and 42° ﬂat plate compression corner models at a Mach number of 4.97. A signiﬁcant increase in heat ﬂux within the separation zone was observed. Furthermore, a bimodal distribution of the power spectral density within the turbulent boundary layer was identiﬁed, with frequencies of approximately 6 kHz and 30 kHz, respectively. Low-frequency predominance, around 0.2 kHz, was noted within the intermittent zone, transitioning to high frequency, approximately 30 kHz, within the separation zone.

title: 高超声速流动中典型构型的激波/湍流边界层干扰及流动控制
abstract_orig: 吸气式高超声速飞行器的内外流场中存在复杂的激波/湍流边界层干扰现象,一旦激波引起流动分离,不仅会造成壁面的气动力/热载荷急剧升高,甚至会诱发非定常流动现象,给飞行器研制带来挑战。高超声速条件下的激波/湍流边界层干扰研究不仅缺乏对经典构型干扰规律的凝练,还缺乏对以内转式进气道为代表的三维复杂构型干扰的模化提炼。本文紧密结合数值模拟、风洞实验和理论方法,围绕高超声速条件下典型构型的激波/湍流边界层干扰的波系结构、流动分离以及流动控制展开研究。针对二维、轴对称和三维扫掠激波/湍流边界层干扰开展了标度律研究,涵盖了宽范围的马赫数、雷诺数和壁温条件。针对压缩拐角和斜激波入射平板二维构型,通过修正壁温对分离准则的影响,建立了高超声速条件下激波/湍流边界层干扰长度的标度律,发现高雷诺数和低雷诺数工况的干扰长度满足不同的标度律,高雷诺数工况的干扰长度相较于低雷诺数工况增长更快。针对圆柱-尾裙和尖锥-尾裙两种构型,建立了轴对称干扰长度的标度律,发现轴对称构型的干扰长度相较于二维构型增长更快。针对立楔-平板构型产生的三维扫掠激波/湍流边界层干扰,通过修正雷诺数的影响,发展了一种适用于宽马赫数和雷诺数范围的上游影响线标度律。针对内转式进气道流动中的三维激波/湍流边界层干扰问题,采用斜激波入射内凹半圆柱面研究模型,在来流马赫数为6的条件下,研究了斜激波的气流偏转角对干扰流场的影响。结果表明,斜激波与内凹半圆柱面干扰产生了以扫掠、入射及反射为主要特征的流动结构。发现斜激波扫掠内凹半圆柱面发生流动分离时,分离激波与入射激波干扰经历了马赫反射向规则反射的转变,利用局部二维化理论,揭示了反射类型转变的机理,并建立了斜激波扫掠内凹半圆柱面上游影响线的标度律。激波扫掠与入射相耦合形成了具有复杂拓扑结构的三维分离区,厘清了分离区内的旋风涡随着气流偏转角的增大而逐渐减小直至消失的演变规律,并建立了斜激波入射内凹半圆柱面干扰长度的标度律。入射激波反射后,上游产生的低能流在对称面对撞并形成流向涡对,揭示了流向涡对向下游发展的演化规律。针对斜激波入射内凹半圆柱面产生的大尺度流动分离,研究了抽吸、扰流片对流动分离的影响。结果表明,在内凹半圆柱面底部开设抽吸缝可以显著减小中心分离区,但难以彻底吸除低能流,其抑制气流汇聚的效果不佳。厘清了抽吸缝几何参数对抽吸效果的影响规律,进而改进了抽吸缝设计。在内凹半圆柱面侧壁安装与扫掠分离线平行的扰流片,可以延迟激波扫掠内凹半圆柱面的分离,通过分析扰流片几何参数对激波扫掠区的影响,揭示了扰流片抑制两侧气流向对称面汇聚的机理。据此提出了抽吸-扰流片组合控制方案,不仅消除了内凹半圆柱面的中心分离区,而且显著降低了出口截面的低能流高度,为三维内转式进气道流动控制提供了重要参考。

title: A study on shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction with varying flow deflection angle
author_display: Surya Prakash Baskaran and T. M. Muruganandam
abstract_orig: Shockwave boundary layer interaction is studied for oblique shocks generated from a shock generator with a varying flow deflection angle. A two-dimensional shock generator with a wedge-shaped geometry is fixed inside the test section and mounted to the wind tunnel’s top wall. The shock generator is made to pitch up and down so that the net flow deflection angle changes because of the pitch motion. As a result, the shock strength changes for a varying flow deflection angle of the shock generator with a fixed incoming Mach number of the flow. The imposed adverse pressure gradient on the boundary layer by this incident shock changes, which influences the shape and structure of the shockwave boundary layer interaction. Three different shockwave boundary layer interaction structures are observed with high-speed schlieren from the experiments conducted for the current study. Schematics for these structures’ types are illustrated, and a model is presented to build the transition criteria for the flow deflection angles for which the transition would take place from one structure to the other. The two transition criteria, one for type 1 to type 2 transition and the other for type 2 to type 3 transition, are validated with the observed results from the experiments. Assumptions made for the transition criteria are also validated with experimental results.

title: 基于振荡式涡流发生器的激波/边界层干扰控制方法
abstract_orig: 激波/边界层干扰（Shock Wave/Boundary Layer Interaction, SWBLI）是高超声速进气道中常见的流动现象，当其诱导边界层发生显著分离时往往会导致进气道气动性能严重下降。为此，本文提出了一种基于新型振荡式涡流发生器阵列的SWBLI控制方法，采用基于动网格技术的非定常仿真方法对该涡流发生器阵列流场进行了研究，验证了该控制方法的有效性，并研究了相关参数的影响规律。研究结果表明，振荡式涡流发生器可在超声速边界层内诱导产生振荡强度可变的涡系结构，增强了边界层流动与高速主流的掺混，同时该涡流发生器振荡过程中独特的“挤压”“抽吸”效应持续对气流进行充能，边界层内速度分布饱满程度显著增加。在控制效果方面，随着涡流发生器振荡频率增加，其对边界层低速气流充能的效果增强，对SWBLI流场的控制效果更加明显，形状因子最高可以降低28%；当激波入射在涡流发生器下游34hv时（其中hv为振荡式涡流发生器最大高度），控制效果最佳，激波诱导边界层分离区长度相比无控制时可减少25%；在涡流发生器下游x=270 mm处截取高度30 mm(z=30 mm)设置为监控面，相比于定几何涡流发生器，监控面总压恢复系数提升5%，马赫数提升2.4%。

title: A scaling analysis for turbulent shock-wave/boundary-layer interactions
author_display: L. J. Souverein, P. G. Bakker and P. Dupont
abstract_orig: A model based on mass conservation properties is developed for shock-wave/boundarylayer interactions (SWBLIs), aimed at reconciling the observed great diversity in ﬂow organization documented in the literature, induced by variations in interaction geometry and aerodynamic conditions. It is the basis for a scaling approach for the interaction length that is valid independent of the geometry of the ﬂow (considering compression corners and incident-reﬂecting shock interactions). As part of the analysis, a scaling argument is proposed for the imposed pressure jump that depends principally on the free-stream Mach number and the ﬂow deﬂection angle. Its interpretation as a separation criterion leads to a successful classiﬁcation of the separation states for turbulent SWBLIs (attached, incipient or separated). In addition, the dependence of the interaction length on the Reynolds number and the Mach numbers is accounted for. A large compilation of available data provides support for the validity of the model. Some general properties on the state of the ﬂow are derived, independent of the geometry of the ﬂow and for a wide range of Mach numbers and Reynolds numbers.

title: Unsteady Motion of Shock Wave for a Supersonic Compression Ramp Flow Based on Large Eddy Simulation
abstract_orig: A large eddy simulation (LES) is conducted to investigate shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interaction in a 24° compression ramp at a high inlet Mach number of M a = 2.9. The recycling/rescaling Method is used as the inflow turbulence generation technique. The shock wave structure and boundary layer flow in the interaction region are studied by flow visualization methods, such as vortex recognition and numerical schlieren. The distributions of turbulent kinetic energy and Reynolds normal stresses at different streamwise locations are analyzed. The results show that a strong anisotropy turbulent flow appears in the reattached boundary layer after the interaction of the shock wave. The large-scale unsteady motion of the separation shock wave is analyzed by using the intermittent factor and power spectrum. It is found that the shock moves around the averaged separation position, and the length scale is equal to 72% of the inlet boundary layer thickness. The power spectrum analysis reveals the existence of low-frequency instability in the separation region.

title: Interaction of a moving shock wave with a turbulent boundary layer
author_display: Patrice S.R. Touré and Erich Schülein
abstract_orig: In the present study, the inﬂuence of a uniformly moving impinging shock on the resulting shock wave–turbulent boundary layer interaction is numerically investigated. The relative Mach number of the shock front travelling above a ﬂat-plate model varied between 0 and 2.3, while the quasi-steady inﬂow conditions remained constant with a Mach number of 3. To quantitatively evaluate the effect of shock travelling speed, a well-known scaling method for interaction length in quasi-steady ﬂows was applied as a reference after signiﬁcant improvements in modelling the effects of Reynolds number and wall temperature using new and existing data. Moreover, previously obtained experimental results for a limited range of travelling speeds were employed to validate the obtained numerical results. Three ranges of shock travelling speeds with distinctly different properties were extracted and quantitatively described using a developed correlation-based approach built on the extended quasi-stationary scaling law. In the ﬁrst range, the scaled interaction length reaches its maximum for the given interaction strength and can be directly described by the scaling law obtained for quasi-stationary interactions. In the second travelling-speed range, the dependence of the interaction length on the interaction strength is explicitly inﬂuenced by the shock movement. With increasing shock travelling speed, the scaled interaction length here decreases signiﬁcantly faster than in the quasi-stationary reference case. The end of this speed range is reached when the absolute shock front speed has caught up with the maximum speed of sound in the interaction zone, and thus the interaction length has fallen to zero. This travelling-speed limit signiﬁes the transition to the third range, where upstream inﬂuence is no longer possible.

title: Scaling for steady and traveling shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interactions
author_display: P. S. R. Touré and E. Schülein
abstract_orig: Shock-wave/boundary-layer interactions (SW–BLIs) play an important role in a wide range of transonic, supersonic and hypersonic applications. Fundamental studies on stationary interactions have been conducted extensively during the last 60 years. However, unsteady SWBLIs with traveling shock fronts have been little studied on canonical geometries. In the present experimental investigation, the influence of a uniformly moving impinging shock on the separated SWBLI flow is analyzed, with a freestream Mach number of 3 and a traveling Mach number in upstream direction of 0.5. To evaluate this effect, stationary reference SWBLIs have been investigated in a wide ranging study. A scaling method from the literature has been enhanced to drastically reduce the data scattering using a new approach accounting for the Reynolds number influence. title: Prediction of separation length for hypersonic shock wave/turbulent boundary layer interactions
abstract_orig: In this study, the physical mechanisms underlying Shock wave/Turbulent Boundary Layer Interactions (STBLI) are investigated and two key factors are identified as governing the separation length: The strength of the incident shock and the intensity of the boundary layer’s shear effect. To quantify these effects, the concepts of disturbance strength and resistance strength are introduced, and their relative difference is defined as the normalized disturbance strength. By applying classical free interaction theory, it is demonstrated that the non-dimensional separation length can be expressed as a function of the normalized disturbance strength. Accordingly, a new model, referred to as the disturbance–resistance model, is proposed for predicting the separation length in STBLI. This model is validated through comprehensive Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) simulations conducted over a wide range of freestream flow parameters. Furthermore, this predictive model provides a clearer physical interpretation of how primary parameters, such as Mach number, Reynolds number, and wall-to-freestream temperature ratio, influence separation behavior of the interaction flows.

title: Research on the flow separation characteristics of shock wave-boundary layer interaction
author_display: Hui Zhang, Deyu Gai and Wei Cao
abstract_orig: Laminar flow separation caused by shock wave-boundary layer interaction is a critical issue for supersonic vehicles, which significantly affects their aerodynamic performance. In-depth studies of the flow separation characteristics and accurate predictions of the separation zone dimensions are essential for optimizing flow control strategies and determining the location of the peak heat flux. This study focuses on the incident shock wave flat plate model and employs direct numerical simulation to investigate the separation flow caused by an incident shock wave-laminar boundary layer under varying shock intensities and wall temperatures. The research results show that with increasing shock intensity, a secondary separation zone appears within the separation region, and the emergence of this secondary zone increases the normal pressure gradient of the primary separation zone. The size of the secondary separation zone first increases, then decreases, and ultimately vanishes as the wall temperature increases. Additionally, based on the Katzer prediction formula, the separation bubble dimension prediction formula was optimized by considering the effects of wall temperature. Experimental and numerical validations demonstrate that the optimized formula can predict the scale of the primary separation zone in the Mach number range of 1.6–15 and wall temperature ratios of 0.2–1. The formula exhibits excellent predictive accuracy under both adiabatic and isothermal wall conditions and remains reliable in accurately predicting the primary separation bubble dimension even in the presence of secondary separation.

title: Dynamics of Three-Dimensional Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interactions
author_display: Datta V. Gaitonde and Michael C. Adler
abstract_orig: Advances in measuring and understanding separated, nominally two-dimensional (2D) shock-wave/turbulent-boundary-layer interactions (STBLI) have triggered recent campaigns focused on three-dimensional (3D) STBLI, which display far greater configuration diversity. Nonetheless, unifying properties emerge for semi-infinite interactions, taking the form of conical asymptotic behavior where shock-generator specifics become insignificant. The contrast between 2D and 3D separation is substantial; the skewed vortical structure of 3D STBLI reflects the essentially 2D influence of the boundary layer on the 3D character of the swept shock. As with 2D STBLI, conical interactions engender prominent spectral content below that of the turbulent boundary layer. However, the uniform separation length scale, which is crucial to normalizing the lowest-frequency dynamics in 2D STBLI, is absent. Comparatively, the spectra of 3D STBLI are more representative of the mid-frequency, convective, shear-layer dynamics in 2D, while phenomena associated with 2D separation-shock breathing are muted. Asymptotic behavior breaks down in many regions important to 3D-STBLI dynamics, occurring in a configuration-dependent manner. Aspects of inceptive regions near shock generators and symmetry planes are reviewed. Focused efforts toward 3D modal and nonmodalanalyses, moving-shock/boundary-layer interactions, fluid/structure interactions, and flow control are suggested as directions for future work.

title: Progress in shock wave/boundary layer interactions
abstract_orig: Recent advances in shock wave boundary layer interaction research are reviewed in four areas: (i) understanding low frequency unsteadiness, (ii) heat transfer prediction capability, (iii) phenomena in complex (multi-shock boundary layer) interactions and (iv) ﬂow control techniques. Substantial success has been achieved in describing the phenomenology of low frequency unsteadiness, including correlations and coherent structures in the separation bubble, through complementary experimental and numerical studies on nominally 2-D interactions. These observations have been parlayed to propose underlying mechanisms based on oscillation, ampliﬁcation and upstream boundary layer effects. For heat transfer prediction capability, systematic studies conducted under the auspices of AFOSR and RTOAVT activities have shown that for axisymmetric laminar situations, heat transfer rates can be measured, and in many cases predicted, reasonably accurately even in the presence of high-temperature effects. Efforts have quantiﬁed uncertainty of Reynolds averaged turbulence models, and hybrid methods have been developed to at least partially address deﬁciencies. Progress in complex interactions encompass two of the major phenomena affected by SBLI in scramjet ﬂowpaths: unstart and mode transition from ramjet (dual mode) to scramjet. Control studies have attempted to leverage the better understanding of the fundamental phenomena with passive and active techniques, the latter exploiting the superior properties of newer actuators. Objectives include reduction in size of the separation region, surface loads and modulation of spectral content. Finally, SBLI studies have beneﬁted handsomely from successful ground and ﬂight test campaigns associated with the HIFiRE-1 and HIFiRE-2 campaigns, results from which are woven into the discussion, as are limitations in current capability and understanding.

title: Historical Review of Experimental Studies and Prediction Methods to Describe Laminar and Turbulent Shock Wave/Boundary Layer Interactions in Hypersonic Flows
journal: 44th AIAA Aerospace Sciences Meeting and Exhibit
publisher: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
abstract_orig: A historical review is presented of studies to examine the characteristics of regions of shock wave/boundary layer interaction in hypersonic flow to develop empirical, analytical and numerical prediction methods to describe these flows. We first review studies, starting in the early 1940s, to understand the flow mechanisms associated with boundary layer separation to develop empirical correlations and boundary layer methods to describe the characteristics of separated regions induced by shock wave/boundary layer interaction. We then discuss studies of separated flows over spiked bodies and indented nose shapes conducted to examine novel solutions for thermal protection systems and as test cases for CFD code validation. The early experimental studies to understand the characteristics of laminar interaction regions are reviewed together with predictions based on integral solutions to the boundary layer equation. Recent experimental studies to generate datasets for CFD validation are compared with the most recent Navier-Stokes and DSMC solutions. Studies to examine the characteristics of shock- and wedge-induced turbulent interaction regions are discussed together with correlations of their major characteristics and NavierStokes predictions. Experimental studies of shock/shock boundary layer interaction are reviewed together with prediction methods. This paper concludes with requirements for future research to develop models to describe effects of flowfield and surface chemistry, wall and shear layer transition, compressibility, shock turbulence interaction, and large-scale unsteadiness on models of turbulence to describe attached and separated regions of shock wave/boundary layer interaction.

title: CRITICAL HYPERSONIC AEROTHERMODYNAMIC PHENOMENA
author_display: John J. Bertin and Russell M. Cummings
abstract_orig: The challenges in understanding hypersonic ﬂight are discussed and critical hypersonic aerothermodynamics issues are reviewed. The ability of current analytical methods, numerical methods, ground testing capabilities, and ﬂight testing approaches to predict hypersonic ﬂow are evaluated. The areas where aerothermodynamic shortcomings restrict our ability to design and analyze hypersonic vehicles are discussed, and prospects for future capabilities are reviewed. Considerable work still needs to be done before our understanding of hypersonic ﬂow will allow for the accurate prediction of vehicle ﬂight characteristics throughout the ﬂight envelope from launch to orbital insertion.
notes: 临界超音速空气热动力现象 摘要：讨论了理解高超音速飞行所面临的挑战，并回顾了关键的高超音速空气热力学问题。 评估了当前分析方法、数值方法、地面测试能力和飞行测试方法预测高超音速流动的能力。 讨论了空气热力学的缺陷在哪些方面限制了我们设计和分析高超声速飞行器的能力，并展望了未来的能力。 在我们对高超音速流动的理解能够准确预测飞行器从发射到进入轨道的整个飞行包络线的飞行特性之前，仍有大量工作要做。 1.INTRODUCTION 在高超音速飞行器的流场中，高温气体效应会对作用在表面的力（压力和表面摩擦力）和能量通量（对流和辐射加热）产生强烈影响。 高超音速气流的特点通常是存在强烈的冲击和平衡或非平衡气体化学反应。 准确预测这些影响对于设计任何以高超音速飞行的飞行器都至关重要。 作用于飞行器表面的压力和表皮摩擦力在整个构型上进行整合，以确定空气动力和力矩（如升力、阻力、俯仰力矩和控制面有效性）。 作为热保护系统（TPS）设计过程的一部分，对飞行器表面的峰值传热速率和加热负荷（即随时间综合的加热速率）进行映射。 评估结构负载和通风环境需要压力分布。 飞行器进入地球大气层时的热传导率峰值出现在空气表现为连续体的高度。 然而，在哥伦比亚号执行 STS-107 飞行任务时，从 91,441 米的进入到 82,297 米的再入大气层期间，温度传感器已经测得了异常高的温度。 这一高度范围内的空气密度相对较低。 平均自由程相对较大。 在超过连续流体区域的海拔高度上，飞行器波后滞止压力常常在0.0001~0.001atm范围内。 2.TOOLS FOR DEFINING THE CONTINUUM, HYPERSONIC AEROTHERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT 从设计过程一开始，设计人员必须确定空气热动力环境的某些 "已知参数 "的值，例如升力、阻力、修正要求、TPS、流场中气体的热化学状态等。 当然，我们无法确定某些已知参数的值，例如，确定边界层过渡发生的位置。 尽管如此，我们应该将这些参数作为一个因素纳入设计。 虽然我们仍无法严格模拟支配这些参数的基本流体力学，但我们可以针对应用估算出它们的值。只有当这些问题是 "未知的未知数 "时，才会成为设计人员/工程师的危机。 2.1 Analytical Methods 对于简单外形迎风面，我们可以假设自由流中气体粒子的速度和方向保持不变，直到它们撞击到固体表面。 对于这种牛顿流动模型，撞击流体粒子动量的法向分量被抹去，而切向分量则保持不变。 局部压力系数方程为 由于压力系数停滞点值的测量值和计算值总是小于 2，Lees（1955 年）提出了高超音速流动压力系数的另一种表示方法，即用流动处驻点压力系数的适当值代替系数 "2"，也即改进牛顿流体理论： 由球形部分组成的迎风面可以使用 Fay & Riddell（1958 年）的方程计算出该构型在零攻击角时达到驻点的加热率。 参考驻点热传导率是指在零迎角时的热传导率。 Lees（1956 年）提出了一个方程，用于确定高超音速流中钝鼻体的传热速率（q）与停滞点距离的函数关系，引入了驻点流动的极限近似值，使用相同的层流边界层方程，配置为零攻角。 将基于相似性的层流边界层传热分布表达式除以驻点传热速率，可得到一个无量纲传热参数，该参数是无量纲热学特性、等效截面半径（Cooke，1961 年）和（Hildebrand，1957 年）以及驻点润湿距离的函数。 从 Fay & Riddell（1958）的研究成果出发，我们可以证明（Bertin 1994），驻点加热率的近似值可以通过以下方法计算得出：（K 是单位常数，RN 是机头半径，ρ1 是自由流密度，V1 是自由流速度，Tt2 是冲击波下游的总温度，Tw 是壁面温度，Zt2 是下游停滞点的压缩系数，Zw,t 是壁面的压缩系数） 2.2 Numerical Methods 使用CFD遇到困难的原因在于高超音速气流中可能出现的复杂流动特征：薄冲击层（高压缩）、由高掠过和弓形激波引起的熵层、粘性/非粘性相互作用以及真实气体效应，包括离解、电离（高温）和稀化（高海拔）；详见 Bertin & Cummings (2003)。Cheng（1993 年）在阐述预测粘性/非粘性相互作用的困难时指出，"高超音速流的流体动力学因边界层和剪切层与冲击波的相互作用而变得复杂，导致流动分离和不稳定性，无法进行直接分析"。从模拟角度来看，Longo 等人（2000 年）的研究表明，至少有五个因素会影响再入飞行器流动预测的准确性。 这些因素包括网格密度、模拟平衡流或非平衡流的能力、模拟转捩和湍流的能力以及精确模拟飞行器几何形状（特别是在激波相互作用区域）所需的工作量。 多年来，已开发出多种重要的数值算法，专门用于处理超音速和高超音速下形成的激波。 大多数方法都属于 "激波捕捉 "方法，即通过求解流体运动方程来确定冲击位置和强度。这些方法可以追溯到 Lax & Wendroff (1960) 的显式方法和 MacCormack (1969) 的预测-修正方案。 预测冲击的另一种方法是莫雷蒂（Moretti，1974 年）提出的 "激波拟合"，即在已知冲击位置后，利用兰金-胡戈尼奥特（Rankine-Hugoniot）激波关系确定激波跃变条件。 尽管激波拟合方法很有吸引力，但多年来开发的绝大多数算法都是激波捕捉算法。激波在许多数值方法中都会引起不稳定性，因此必须使用某种上风差分或通过明确添加数值平滑来处理不稳定性的算法。 遗憾的是，抑制激波所需的数值耗散往往会降低对边界层或涡流等粘性现象的预测。 在过去的几十年中，网格生成技术取得了长足的进步，许多商用程序都能很好地创建复杂几何形状的网格，但高超音速流动的高难度要求会让最好的网格生成软件也吃不消。 创建复杂的网格仍然需要数周甚至数月的时间，尤其是在概念设计阶段考虑各种配置的情况。 表面几何定义和网格生成仍然是 CFD 过程中的最大瓶颈。 网格敏感性研究对高超音速下的精确流动预测尤为重要，而单元雷诺数对结果尤为重要： "在停滞点附近，即使是 10 级的较小单元雷诺数值也可能导致 100% 的误差，而当单元雷诺数值小于或等于 3 时，热通量就会收敛"。 很少有模型是专门针对高速流动而开发的，要对这些高速气流进行正确建模，需要加入可压缩耗散和压力膨胀修正。CFD 模拟中最常用的非平衡模型可能是 Park（1989 年）的双温模型。 该模型使用平移温度和振动温度，以及关于气体种类的平移、旋转、振动和电子激发模式的各种假设。如对预测非平衡流动的困难的更多细节感兴趣，可参阅 Park（1990 年）关于非平衡高超声速流动的著作和 Bird（1994 年）关于直接模拟气体流动的著作。 2.3 Ground-Based Tests 目前的设计过程中用于确定空气热力学环境的大部分测量数据，即空气动力和力矩、表面压力分布和热传导分布，都是通过以下方法获得的：1. 传统风洞； 2. 激波加热风洞； 3. 激波管； 4. 电弧加热试验设备； 5. 弹道自由飞行试验场。 地面测试设施可模拟的参数包括：1. 自由流马赫数； 2. 自由流雷诺数（及其对边界层特性的影响）； 3. 自由流速度；4.压力高度；5.流体的总焓；6.激波的密度比；7.测试气体；8.壁面与总温度比；9.流场的热化学。但是我们无法同时模拟所有参数。 还要注意的是，在风洞试验程序的具体运行过程中，模型温度通常从室温开始。 用于确定模型热传导率的温度测量通常在测试运行初期进行。 因此，在试验过程的数据记录部分，模型表面的温度相对较低。 另一方面，由于长时间暴露在高温飞行环境中，飞行器表面会变得非常热。 因此，地面测试中的壁温与总温之比通常远低于飞行值。 为了使壁温与总温之比符合飞行值，隧道内气流的总温度会降低到飞行值以下。 开展地面试验项目有许多原因。 其中包括以下原因：1. 获取数据，以确定复杂流场无法进行计算建模的完整构型的空气动力和力矩和/或传热分布。2. 利用部分构型获取数据，确定局部流动现象，如高超音速喷气发动机的入口流场，或与偏转控制面（如襟翼）相关的冲击/边界层相互作用。 3. 获取详细的流场数据，用于开发计算算法的数值模型（代码验证）。 4. 获取热传导和阻力等参数的测量数据，用于在一系列构型几何和流动条件下与计算流场解决方案进行比较（代码校准）。 5. 获取数据，用于对无法进行分析和/或数值建模的现象（如边界层过渡和湍流建模）建立经验相关性，并对喷气发动机的性能进行认证。 2.4 Flight Tests Neumann (1989) 认为，进行飞行试验有多种原因。 Buck 等人（1963 年）提出的四个原因是：1. 展示技术，发现意想不到的问题； 2. 成为技术的催化剂（或焦点）； 3. 不仅从飞行中，而且从开发过程中获得知识；以及 4. 在飞行中展示技术，使其在更大规模的应用中具有可信度。 Neumann 补充了他自己的三个理由： 5. 验证地面测试数据和/或了解地面测试模拟与实际飞行之间的桥梁； 6. 验证系统的整体性能；以及 7. 生成地面无法获得的信息。 飞行试验计划分为两类：(1) 研究与开发 (R & D) 计划；(2) 原型或运行飞行器的飞行。 研发计划侧重于技术问题，这推动了飞行器的设计及其飞行操作。已经获得了的飞行测试数据，例如无人驾驶的 Apollo Command Modules 017 和 020 的飞行，如 Lee 和 Goodrich（1972 年）所讨论的，以及运行飞行器的飞行测试数据，例如航天飞机轨道器（Bertin 1994 年，Bertin 等 1996 年）。 Throckmorton（1992）指出，将航天飞机轨道器作为飞行研究飞行器，作为其正常运行任务的辅助工具，是整个 20 世纪 70 年代研究界讨论的一个话题。 根据从嵌入航天飞机 TPS 的热电偶获得的飞行测试数据得出的空气热力学参数被用来扩大轨道器的飞行范围。 Hodge & Audley （1983 年）指出："该技术的要求包括：模拟热量传递到 TPS 上某一点的分析模型；使嵌入 TPS 表面附近的热电偶的响应充分高于噪声水平的飞行试验操作；以及用于减少飞行热电偶数据的参数估计程序 ......数据缩减程序将加热与攻角、侧滑、控制面偏转和雷诺数等变量相关联。 这项技术也可用于风洞数据缩减"。 撞击激波和弓形激波之间的相互作用会产生局部严重的热传递率。 Edney（1968b）确定了六种不同的激波/激波相互作用模式。 轨道器襟翼的正偏转产生激波，与轨道器上的边界层相互作用。 激波产生的不利压力梯度导致边界层增厚，并在许多情况下导致边界层分离。 相互作用产生的扰动的上游范围取决于接近边界层的亚音速部分的大小和气流转向产生的激波的强度。 因此，正如 Bertin（1994 年）所指出的，影响相互作用范围的参数有：(1) 接近边界层是层流还是湍流；(2) 接近气流的马赫数；(3) 接近气流的雷诺数；(4) 表面温度；(5) 斜坡的偏转角；(6) 气体的化学状态。 Bertin 等人（1996 年）和 Fujii 等人（2001 年）利用高超音速飞行期间测得的传热实验值研究了偏转控制面引起的扰动流场。 HYFLEX 飞行器（Fujii 等人，2001 年）是一种小型研发飞行器，长度为 4.40 米（14.44 英尺）。 两级发射器以 3.88 千米/秒（12.73 千英尺/秒）的速度提供 107 千米（351 千英尺）的初始高度。 边界层转捩是数据收集工作的重点。 Weston 和 Fitzkee（1963 年）指出，“在水星座舱上观测到的边界层转捩雷诺数与在超高速喷枪设施中飞行的球体后的尾流过渡雷诺数非常吻合"。 20 世纪 60 年代还试飞了再入飞行器 F，该飞行器提供了高超音速边界层转换，至今仍在使用。 再入 F 飞行器提供了马赫数高达 20 和高度低至 24.38 千米（80.00 千英尺）的边界层过渡数据（Wright 和 Zoby，1977 年）。 总结：尽管对高超音速流动进行了数十年的研究，但在分析和设计高速飞行器方面仍然存在许多挑战。 最近发生的 "哥伦比亚 "号事故就清楚地表明，在高超音速飞行领域仍然存在 "未知的未知数"，即使是我们最好的实验或数值分析也无法充分预测。 由于高超音速风洞无法充分模拟飞行器的马赫数、雷诺数和高焓状态，我们只能对测试数据进行近似和推断。 我们在计算模拟中模拟化学反应以及充分预测诸如激波-激波相互作用等流动特征的能力还存在不确定性，因此还需要做更多的工作，才能使 CFD 对高超音速流动的预测完全可信。 飞行试验仍然昂贵而危险，这对我们耗费资源探索未知世界的意愿提出了挑战。 了解高超音速流动对研究人员的挑战由来已久，毫无疑问，在未来很长一段时间内，我们都将面临挑战。

title: Hypersonics into the 21st century: A perspective on AFOSR-sponsored research in aerothermodynamics
abstract_orig: This paper documents the programmatic context and considerations that have shaped the development and execution of a number of research initiatives implemented by the Air Force Ofﬁce of Scientiﬁc Research Aerothermodynamics and Turbulence portfolio since 2001. The National Hypersonic Foundational Research Plan has been developed in concert with NASA and Sandia National Laboratories to coordinate strategic planning in the scientiﬁc disciplines relevant to hypersonic technologies. The HIFiRE program has provided ﬂight data to provide insight into the behavior of critical phenomena in-ﬂight and helped address several key objectives identiﬁed in the National Hypersonic Foundational Research Plan. The STAR initiative facilitated the transition of knowledge and capabilities from basic research to technology development and has made key contributions to national-scale programs and Test and Evaluation capabilities. In the future the portfolio will focus on energy transfer mechanisms between kinetic, internal and chemical modes as a potential approach to new ﬂow control capabilities and to expand the contributions of the portfolio to other areas of interest to the Air Force.
notes: 摘要：本文记录了空军科学研究实验室（AFOSR）在空气热力学和湍流的联合学科自 2001 年以来实施的一系列研究计划的制定和执行的计划背景和考虑因素。 国家高超音速基础研究计划是与美国国家航空航天局和桑迪亚国家实验室共同制定的，旨在协调与高超音速技术相关的科学学科的战略规划。 HIFiRE 计划提供了飞行数据，使人们能够深入了解飞行中关键现象的行为，并帮助实现国家高超声速基础研究计划中确定的几个关键目标。 STAR 计划促进了知识和能力从基础研究向技术开发的过渡，并为国家级计划和测试与评估能力做出了重要贡献。 未来，该研究组合将重点关注动能、内部和化学模式之间的能量传递机制，以此作为实现新的流动控制能力的潜在方法，并将该研究组合的贡献扩大到空军感兴趣的其他领域。 高超声速能力是一种颠覆性的能力，而且能带来很好的经济效益。这种武器能具备快速反应、难以打击的特点。下图是一个不同马赫数能覆盖的15min射程区域图。 高超音速能力的实现在很大程度上取决于各学科的进步。 已经飞行的有动力高超音速系统主要是高度集成的升力体，其空气动力和推进功能相互依存，而无动力重返大气层系统的热保护需要考虑空气热力学、材料响应和结构载荷等多学科因素。 同样，推进高超音速能力所面临的科学挑战也需要整合流体动力学、热物理学、高温材料、化学和计算科学等多个科学学科的贡献。 空气热力学环境定义了边界条件，这些边界条件推动了科学挑战和许多这些学科的参数空间。 因此，高效、准确地预测空气热力学基态的能力成为提高系统设计和分析能力的关键驱动力。 目前的高超声速科学会分为两个组别：系统集成相关的工程挑战，未知热物理现象的科学挑战。 额定的热化学过程决定了能量从激发的内部状态释放为热能，对空气热力学的准确预测则取决于所需的相关反应速率的准确性。 在这一区域内，非平衡气体环境与反应材料表面之间的相互作用的预测取决于对气体中、气体表面界面以及材料近表面区域内发生的基本热化学反应速率的准确了解。 AFOSR 空气热力学和湍流组合负责高速和高能流相关的流体动力学研究，目前的重点领域包括湍流和边界层的基础物理学、激波主导的流动--特别是激波/边界层和激波-激波的相互作用，以及热化学非平衡中的流动。 一些国外对推动高超声速飞行研究做出的举措： 1、HIFiRE - the Hypersonic International Flight Research and Experimentation. 高超声速全球飞行研究和实验中心。 2、STAR - the STability Analysis for Reentry. 再入大气层的稳定性分析。 3、NHFRP - the National Hypersonic Foundational Research Plan. 4、Basic research initiatives in the integration of aerothermodynamic, high-temperature materials, and high-temperature chemistry research and the identification and exploitation of fundamental mechanisms of energy transfer that influence the macroscopic behavior of high-speed flows. HIFiRE 计划是一个多次飞行、经济高效的飞行项目，其目标是接受更大的技术风险，以促进关键科学数据的收集，从而影响未来项目的发展。马克-刘易斯（Mark Lewis）博士是该计划的主要启发者和倡导者之。一个过去的例子是 X-15 计划，该计划在 199 次飞行过程中为高超音速能力的发展提供了关键的基础知识--有时是通过飞行失败获得的。 昆士兰大学的 Allan Paull 教授是该计划的首席研究员。 Paull 的HyShot 学术喷气式火箭飞行研究项目跨越了以往只有通过政府项目才能进行飞行研究的模式，并激发了对小型、经济实惠的探空火箭所能实现的目标的思考。Fisher 和Dougherty 研究了地面试验设施中的扰动水平对锥体上层流-湍流过渡的作用，并将这些结果与同一模型的飞行数据进行了比较，为科学驱动的飞行研究开创了令人印象深刻的先例。HIFiRE 计划由九次研究飞行和一次低风险飞行组成，前者旨在应对各种高超音速科学挑战，后者旨在解决飞行器姿态控制问题。 Dolvin 对计划进行了全面总结，Kimmel和Adamczak 则对计划的空气热力学目标进行了回顾。HIFiRE research flight 1 and 5是专门用于气动热力学研究的。 与高超音速系统开发相关的两个关键科学挑战是层流-湍流过渡的精确估算和冲击/边界层相互作用的不稳定性建模。 这两种现象都是空气热动力加热或声学载荷的重要来源，对飞行器结构的设计有很大影响。 以前的研究还没有对飞行中冲击/边界层相互作用的基本不稳定性进行过研究，而且在飞行雷诺数下进入的边界层的作用和相互作用的动力学方面还存在未解决的问题。 HIFiRE 计划在延续 HyShot 和 HyCAUSE 的传统以及塑造当前经济高效的飞行研究理念方面发挥了重要作用。 HIFiRE飞行的成功率，以及与HIFiRE有着类似理念基础的德国航天中心SHEFEX 项目的成功率，令新一代的主要高超声速技术演示项目中出现了较小规模的风险缓解飞行研究部分。 此外，弗吉尼亚大学/弗吉尼亚理工大学High-V项目等由学术界主导的飞行研究项目也在不断涌现。 层流-湍流过渡的预测存在很大的不确定性，对系统热保护系统有很大影响。开发和过渡易于实施并与现有工业设计流程相结合的先进数值方法，并向支持猎鹰（Falcon）计划的应用研究机构和行业提供层流-湍流过渡专题专家， 这项工作被命名为 STAR 再入大气层稳定性分析。 基于线性稳定性理论或抛物面稳定性方程 (PSE) 的研究方法可预测基本平均流解决方案中不稳定性的增长，几十年来一直被科学界所采用，但在技术成熟方面似乎缺乏认可。 在 AFOSR 的赞助下，明尼苏达大学的 Johnson 和 Candler 开发了一种名为 PSECHEM 的 PSE 方法，其中包括在分析中考虑有限速率气体化学效应的功能。 虽然当时在研究界还有其他几种 PSE 方法在使用，其中最著名的是 NASA LASTRAC 代码，但 PSECHEM 包括了对高超声速流动分析至关重要的气体化学效应，这促使他们选择 PSECHEM 作为技术过渡计划的基础。 Johnson 率先将 PSECHEM 重新配置为一个易于集成、用户友好的稳定性分析工具，以便过渡到应用研究领域。 我们投入了大量精力，以确保该工具可以随时安装并与现有的计算求解器集成，同时确保代码可以在培训或开发模式下运行，并具有易于理解的图形用户界面。 Johnson 还花费了大量时间支持潜在用户的安装和教育工作。 由此产生的工具被重新命名为 STABL（边界层稳定性分析），并在 STAR 团队对 HTV-2 和 X-51 项目分析的贡献中得到利用和完善。 与此同时，Candler 的研究小组开发了美国国家航空航天局高超音速工作母机 DPLR（Data Parallel Line Relaxation 数据平行线松弛） 的改进非结构化版本，该版本最初由Wright和Candler开发。 新的非结构化代码被称为 US3D，它结合了动能保护通量重构，以提高小振幅波动的分辨率，同时保留低阶算法的计算效率。 US3D 的设计目的是便于与 STABL 和其他专门的配套求解器耦合，以解决气体-表面相互作用和烧蚀等多物理现象。 在 STAR 计划启动之初，人们曾设想，一旦团队展示的先进方法对技术开发界的益处显而易见，这些方法和工具就会在工业界和政府实验室内迅速得到采用。 遗憾的是，事实并非如此，几年来，STAR 计划主要是作为主要技术示范计划的支持项目而存在。 US3D 用于模拟模型上的平均流，STABL 则利用模拟结果来确定流场内最有可能出现的不稳定机制。 目前有三个 RTO (NATO Research and Technology Organisation)小组，分别研究催化气体-表面相互作用（AVT-199）、高超音速系统中的空气热源（AVT-205）和高超音速层流-湍流过渡（AVT-200），它们也是在 AVT-136 的工作基础上发展起来的。 Michael Holden博士领导的 CUBRC 团队提供的实验数据对这些活动以及其他各种活动的成功起到了至关重要的作用。 霍尔登的团队负责对双锥流场进行了多项实验研究，在高焓流非平衡效应的表征和模拟、各种飞行演示构型的关键气动现象评估以及 HIFiRE 飞行 1 和 5 构型的初步实验分析方面取得了进展。 虽然此前曾有过几次在全国范围内协调高超音速研究的努力，但国家高超音速基础研究计划的意图是采用一种略有不同的方法，重点关注科学而非技术方面的挑战。 国家高超音速飞行计划的六个重点领域：1、边界层物理。2、激波主导的流动。3、非平衡流动。4、超声速燃烧。5、环境、结构和材料的相互作用。6、高温材料和结构。 研究局空气热力学与湍流组合能够指导科研界并促进技术过渡、促进创新科学的发现和发展，并有可能带来变革。 该组合的未来研究重点：气体中动能、内能和化学能之间的能量转移，以及如何在分子和中观尺度上对这种机制进行表征、建模和控制，从而在宏观子系统或飞行器尺度上对流动行为进行管理。 最近在空气热力学方面取得的许多进展都是基于对各种模式--动能、内能或化学能--之间能量传递的新认识。 这方面工作的四个例子包括：Saric 利用离散跨向粗糙度元素控制横流不稳定性[34]；Rasheed 等人利用声吸收表面控制二模不稳定性[35]；Martin 和 Candler 模拟化学反应对边界层内湍流波动的影响[36]；Leyva 等人研究二氧化碳对二模不稳定性衰减的作用[37]。 Saric 控制后掠翼横流不稳定性的方法是在机翼前缘附近的亚临界跨度波数处放置离散有限扰动元件。 该方法采用了多种扰动配置，包括粗糙度、孔洞和等离子致动器。 控制概念背后的基本理论是，亚临界间距元素对基流的扰动会促进相关亚临界不稳定性的发展，从而阻碍临界不稳定性的发展。 这种有利于最良性不稳定性的流场调整利用了流动中各种不稳定模式之间的竞争，在新的程序范例中，可被视为一种有利于将动能分配到对所需流动状态最有利的模式中的方法。 Candler 和 Martin 研究了湍流边界层中内热和放热反应的作用，并注意到随着放热反应中能量的释放，湍流波动强度会增加，而相反，内热反应会导致湍流强度降低。 这项工作说明了流场中化学能和动能模式之间相互作用的潜力。 Hornung 和 Rasheed 的研究通过实验验证了 Malmuth 和 Federov 的理论预测，即可以利用吸声表面来减弱高超音速边界层内的秒模不稳定性。 Hornung 和 Rasheed 通过在锥体的一侧覆盖盲孔作为声学阻尼器，而将另一侧留作光滑表面的方法证明，锥体带孔一侧的过渡雷诺数比光滑一侧高出近 50%。 随后，Bres 等人[38] 采用综合理论和计算方法研究了这一现象，并验证了盲孔对第二模式不稳定性衰减的影响。 在能量传递机制方面，这项研究说明了控制不稳定性内动能的可用性对延迟过渡的影响，从而塑造了流场的宏观状态。 最后，Leyva 等人[37]研究了二氧化碳的存在对锥体的二模不稳定性（second-mode instabilities）的影响。 在早期的实验中，加州理工学院的Hornung研究小组试图解释二氧化碳气流与空气和 N2 气流在锥体上的转换雷诺数相差约 4 倍的现象[39]。理论上，这种效应是二氧化碳中发生二模不稳定性和分子声吸收的光谱范围重叠的结果，因为这种重叠在空气中不会发生。 后来 Jewell 等人[51]的实验表明，在马赫数为 5 的自由流空气边界层中注入二氧化碳，在某些条件下可以延迟过渡的开始时间，Wagnild 和 Candler [40]的模拟验证了注入二氧化碳导致的过渡延迟是二氧化碳内部振动模式吸收第二模式不稳定性能量的结果。 在这种情况下，从不稳定性动能到气体内部振动模式的能量转移导致了锥体边界层过渡位置的延迟。 锥体上空气、二氧化碳和 N2 title: Rate Effects in Hypersonic Flows
abstract_orig: Hypersonic ﬂows are energetic and result in regions of high temperature, causing internal energy excitation, chemical reactions, ionization, and gassurface interactions. At typical ﬂight conditions, the rates of these processes are often similar to the rate of ﬂuid motion. Thus, the gas state is out of local thermodynamic equilibrium and must be described by conservation equations for the internal energy and chemical state. Examples illustrate how competition between rates in hypersonic ﬂows can affect aerodynamic performance, convective heating, boundary layer transition, and ablation. The conservation equations are outlined, and the most widely used models for internal energy relaxation, reaction rates, and transport properties are reviewed. Gas-surface boundary conditions are described, including ﬁniterate catalysis and slip effects. Recent progress in the use of ﬁrst-principles calculations to understand and quantify critical gas-phase reactions is discussed. An advanced ﬁnite-rate carbon ablation model is introduced and is used to illustrate the role of rate processes at hypersonic conditions.
notes: Rate Effects in Hypersonic Flows 摘要：高超音速气流能量大，会产生高温区域，导致内能激发、化学反应、电离和气体表面相互作用。 在典型的飞行条件下，这些过程的速率通常与流体运动的速率相似。 因此，气体状态脱离了局部热力学平衡，必须用内能和化学状态守恒方程来描述。 举例说明了高超音速气流中速率之间的竞争如何影响气动性能、对流加热、边界层过渡和烧蚀。 概述了守恒方程，并回顾了最广泛使用的内能弛豫、反应速率和传输特性模型。 介绍了气体-表面边界条件，包括精细催化和滑移效应。 讨论了使用第一原理计算来理解和量化临界气相反应的最新进展。 介绍了先进的有限速率碳烧蚀模型，并用来说明速率过程在高超声速条件下的作用。 1.INTRODUCTION: THE HYPERSONIC FLOW ENVIRONMENT 最近的一篇文章（Leyva 2017）讨论了当前高超音速空气动力学和空气热力学的许多研究领域。 另一篇最新文章回顾了与scramjets运行相关的关键流体动力学问题（Urzay 2018）。 一篇较早的行星进入气体动力学综述也与此相关（Gnoffo 1999）。 高超音速导致包裹飞行器的冲击层和存在极端剪切力的边界层温度很高。高超音速气流中的高温引起了许多过程，如振动和电子能量激发、化学反应、电离和气体表面相互作用。 当这些过程发生时，完美气体激波关系不再有效，状态方程也变得不简单。 例如，马赫数为 6 的正激波产生的条件是振动能被激发到总内能的 10%左右。振动激发和化学反应的速率取决于局部热力学状态，这些速率随着密度和温度的增加而增加。 在典型的超音速条件下，这些速率通常与平流速率相似。 典型高超声速环境： 考虑高度为 40 千米的情况，有一个强烈的激波将自由流与包裹球-锥几何体的高温气体分开。 这种激波通常被称为弓形激波（bow shock），在中心线上，船首冲击波是正激波的，其强度随中心线距离的增加而减弱。 在这一区域，激波会将气体加热到大约 6,000 K ；这比完全气体正激波理论所预测的 12,300 K 的温度要低得多。这主要是由于内能激发、化学反应和电离造成的，它们吸收能量并降低波后温度。在激波后面的高压区，气体处于局部热力学平衡状态。 然而，在 s/R = 2 时，气体状态是非平衡状态，存在的 N 原子量比平衡状态预测的多四个数量级。 这种失衡或非平衡状态是气体在物体周围迅速膨胀的结果。 压力和温度的下降导致化学重组率突然降低，气体近似冻结在波后热化学状态附近。 因此，反应速率和平流速率之间存在竞争；这是高超音速气流的主要特征之一。 在 60 千米高度，流场大致相似，但冲击波后的高温区更明显，波后的温度更高，达到约 11,400 K。振动电子模式接近平衡，直到气体膨胀，然后 Tve 滞后于 T 的变化。 这些差异是由于该高度的压力和密度较低，导致内能弛豫和化学反应速率降低。 在 80 千米高度，流场明显不同，弓形激波更加分散，温度升高区域较大。 脱体激波距离也明显增大。 在提取流线上的所有位置，振动-电子温度都落后于平移-旋转温度。 解离水平大大降低，在 s/R = 2 时，N 原子和 O 原子的数量比平衡状态下预测的要少。 这是由于低密度自由流条件抑制了反应速率，导致整个流场的反应水平处于亚平衡状态。 平移-旋转温度一般用 T表示，振动-电子温度一般用 Tve表示。 假定气体分子的旋转能量模式与平移或热能模式处于平衡状态，允许振动模式和电子模式中的内能以自己的速率演化，其能量以 Tve 表征。 这是气体能量状态的双温表示法。 在 40 千米处，与非催化表面相比，催化边界条件使停滞点热流量增加了 64%。 这是因为当原子在表面上重新结合时，化学键能量会沉积在表面上。 请注意，在 40 千米的非催化情况下，表面有大量的 O 原子和百分之几的 N 原子，而在催化情况下，这些物质在表面的质量分数接近于零。在 60 千米处，表面催化的影响比 40 千米处要大一些，相对于非催化传热速率增加了 69%。 在 80 千米处，由于解离程度很低，催化和非催化情况下没有明显的差异。 在低自由流密度下，几乎没有解离。 在高密度下，原子组分在低温边界层中重新结合，从而降低了表面催化作用的效果。 平板上的传热系数是气相重组率和表面催化活性的函数。 对于催化表面，热通量与重组速率无关；如果表面是非催化的，且重组速度较慢，则热通量会明显下降。 解离源项与密度成比例关系，而重组与密度的平方成比例关系。 因此，解离和重组的相对重要性会随着自由流密度的变化而改变。 还应注意的是，流场温度随来流速度的平方变化，因此与温度相关的速率 kf 和 kb 随自由流速度平方的变化而变化。 弓形激波后的解离和振动弛豫速率会随着自由流密度的降低而减小。 然而，重组过程对密度的依赖性更强。 当气体突然在头锥和锥体周围膨胀时，密度会降低，重组速率也会随密度的降低而呈二次方下降。 这就是为什么在气流膨胀过程中重组很少，以及为什么 60 千米处的化学凝固比 40 千米处更强的原因。 相比之下，由于振动弛豫是一个二元碰撞过程，因此它更接近于平移温度的变化。 在 40 千米处，密度足够高，热边界层中会发生显著的重组。 在 60 千米处，密度较低，重组减少。 这就是图 4 所示的非催化传热速率与密度的关系。 气表反应的比例关系不像气相反应那么明显。 例如，根据 O + O(s) → O2，考虑氧的催化重组；这里，O(s)是与开放表面位点结合的氧原子。 这一过程的速率并不简单，因为它与气相中的 O 原子浓度和结合到表面的 O 原子数量成正比。 通常，表面覆盖率取决于表面温度和气体压力。 在 Damkohler 数字较大的情况下，过程将接近平衡，而较小的数值则表明过程处于冻结状态。 3.TRANSLATIONAL AND ROTATIONAL PROCESSES 平移非平衡的一个明显例子发生在强冲击波中。 冲击前的速度分布函数具有较小的热分量和较大的自由流方向分量。 冲击后的情况恰恰相反，大部分上游方向的运动转化为热运动。 在冲击波本身内部，速度分布函数要复杂得多，具有冲击前和冲击后分布函数的特征。 这种双峰速度分布函数不能表示为扰动麦克斯韦分布，正如纳维-斯托克斯方程的查普曼-恩斯科格推导所假定的那样。 因此，纳维-斯托克斯方程无法正确表示冲击波内的流动。 同样，波兹曼方程的高阶查普曼-恩斯科格解法（如伯内特方程）也无法表示这种效应。 当平移能量弛豫非常重要时，必须使用基于动力学理论的方法，如直接模拟蒙特卡洛法（Bird，1994 年；Boyd & Schwartzentruber，2017 年）。 这发生在稀薄条件下，可以使用梯度长度的局部克努森数来识别（Boyd 等人，1995 年）： 如果该值超过约 0.05，则纳维-斯托克斯方程可能无效。 通常情况下，旋转能量松弛不需要单独考虑，因为它只对纳维-斯托克斯方程已经可疑或无效的流动有重要意义。 这是因为旋转模态的松弛速度非常快（大约在五到十次碰撞中），而这一速度与平移模态松弛到平衡状态的速度相似。 振动模式则不然。 4. VIBRATIONAL PROCESSES 气体振动模式相对缓慢的弛豫会以多种方式与气体动力学相互作用。 振动模式在活跃时会吸收能量并改变激波后的条件。 气体的振动状态对其解离速率也有很大影响。 振动冷冻和热非平衡在快速膨胀的气流中非常重要，例如在行星进入舱的尾部或高超音速风洞喷管中。 在某些气流中，振动弛豫率可能会根据声学干扰进行调整，从而导致高温气体中声音的消散和扩散。 只要温度足够大，振动模式被激发，就会产生明显的阻尼。振动和旋转过程的弛豫时间差别很大，因此，要获得有效的阻尼，弛豫过程必须与相关声学频率共振。 边界层过渡取决于自由流总焓和气体特性（Adam，1997 年；Adam & Hornung，1997 年；Germain & Hornung，1997 年）。 基于边界层参考温度的过渡雷诺数随着总焓的增加而增加，随着内能激发和化学反应的增加而增加。 此外，二氧化碳的过渡雷诺数比空气或 N2 中的过渡雷诺数大一个数量级。 在这些条件下，边界层过渡是通过 Mack 第二模式（Mack 1975）发生的，这是边界层中的一种声学扰动。 T5 条件下的线性稳定性理论表明，在某些条件下，振动能量松弛和化学反应会导致不稳定增长率降低。 此外，数值实验表明，放热（释放热量）的有限速率过程会增加不稳定增长率，吸热过程则会减少。这表明，在高超声速边界层中，速率过程与第二模式扰动的增长之间可能存在相互作用。 与非反应流相比，放热反应明显更不稳定，而内热反应则有阻尼。 Fujii 和 Hornung（2001 年）的研究表明，在实验条件下，最不稳定的声学频率与二氧化碳的振动弛豫率之间存在重叠。 在此基础上，Leyva 等人（2009 年）和 Jewell 等人（2013 年）研究了向高超音速锥体的边界层注入二氧化碳，试图延迟向湍流的过渡。研究表明，通过精心注入，可以稳定边界层。 Wagnild & Candler（2014 年）利用直接数值模拟研究了高超声速边界层的声学扰动调谐。 这项工作的结果与理论结果一致，说明了振动弛豫调谐对声学扰动的影响。 关于高超音速边界层包括速率效应的研究还有很多；然而，关注振动速率过程及其与声学模式相互作用的研究却很少（例如，Hudson 等人，1997 年；Knisely & Zhong，2018 年）。 还有许多学者研究了平衡气体模型和化学非平衡过程的影响。 然而，化学速率过程比高超音速边界层中的相关扰动要慢得多，而且不能根据相关扰动频率进行调整。 声波的振动阻尼存在三种情况： (a) 平衡，在这种情况下，振动状态迅速适应声波干扰（发生在低频时）；(b) 非平衡，在这种情况下，振动模式以相位滞后的方式响应声波干扰的通过，从而吸收声波模式的能量；(c) 冻结，在这种情况下，声波时间尺度远小于振动弛豫时间尺度，不响应波的通过，因此声波阻尼可以忽略不计。 在低温（300 K）下，声波模式仅被微弱激发，弛豫时间比声波的特征时间慢得多。因此振动模式没有响应并被冻结。 例如，室温空气就是这种情况。 在 1,000 K 时，二氧化碳的弯曲模式被激发（θv = 960 K），其弛豫时间接近声学阻尼的最佳频率。 在这种情况下，振动能量被激发，其响应与平移-旋转温度不同步，从而产生强烈的声学阻尼。 在较高温度下，振动能接近平衡，并迅速响应声波引起的温度扰动。 5.CHEMICAL REACTIONS 解离是高超音速气流中的一个重要过程。 解离过程比较复杂，其速率取决于振动激发水平；振动激发的分子解离的能量障碍较低，更容易解离。 此外，当振动激发的分子解离时，它们会从振动能量池中移除，从而抑制气体混合物的整体振动能量。 振动和解离之间的耦合关系早在 20 世纪 60 年代就已为人所知，并被推测出模型来表示这一过程（如 Marrone 和 Treanor，1963 年）。 这些模型使有效解离率成为 T 和 Tv 的函数。 以前的模型把反应速率作为给定值，然后建立解离模型。 这种方法是不可行的，因为推断出的反应速率取决于用来推断反应速率的模型。 Park （1986 年，1987 年）的分析产生了 √(TTv) 模型，在该模型中，阿伦尼乌斯形式的反应速率在等于 √(TTv) 的有效温度下进行评估。 当 Tv 较低时，该模型会抑制解离速率，这与对解离过程的理解是一致的（如 Hornung 1972a）。 Park 假设 ev,s = 0.3De ，其中 De 是分子的解离能。 这个值是不正确的，会引起数值问题，在实际应用中， ev,s 通常近似为平均振动能。 Park 模型现在被广泛使用，并不是因为它被证明是准确的，而是因为它比许多其他模型更容易实现。 随后，人们又提出了其他模型（如 Knab 等人，1995 年；Luo 等人，2018 年；Singh & Schwartzentruber，2018 年）。 6. SURFACE PROCESSES 气体表面速率过程会对高超音速飞行器的传热速率产生影响。 烧蚀比表面催化重组复杂得多。 最简单的烧蚀表面是某种形式的碳，如石墨或碳-碳基体。 发生的基本反应包括氧化和氮化、表面催化重组以及高温下的升华。 一个有代表性的气体表面动力学模型是（Zhluktov 和 Abe，1999 年）：（ (s) 表示开放的键位，O(s) 表示占据键位的 O 原子，C(b) 表示大块或固体碳原子。 这些过程中的每个过程的速率都是封闭模型所必需的。） 直到最近，这种有限速率模型还没有用于分析，而是采用了气表平衡近似法。 在这种情况下，在表面压力和温度下计算空气和表面材料混合物的平衡成分；这为气相边界条件提供了表面状态。 这种方法通常称为 B′法（无量纲吹气速率），在接近平衡的高压下有效，但在中低压下不太可能有效。 下图显示了使用三种模型对烧蚀进行的 CFD 模拟：平衡 B′方法、Zhluktov 和 Abe（1999 年）的有限速率模型以及最近开发的有限速率模型（Poovathingal 等人，2017 年）。 有限速率模型之间的主要区别在于，相对于二氧化碳，最新模型更倾向于形成一氧化碳；这与氧分子束实验（Murray 等，2015 年）一致。 这里使用了石墨的特性，并在气体和固体之间的界面上求解了气体-表面的质量和能量平衡， 其中包括材料的热反应，以及由于烧蚀质量损失而导致的主体形状变化。 显然，模型之间存在很大差异，相对于有限速率模型，平衡 B′模型产生的衰退要大得多。 Zhluktov和Abe（1999）模型产生的衰退程度最低。 实验（Alba 等，2016 年）表明该模型存在缺陷，而第三个模型与数据更为一致。无论如何，有限速率模型在这些条件下产生的表面衰退程度大大降低了。 此外，模型预测的边界层组成也完全不同，边界层内能动力学会产生重要影响。 要全面验证模型，还需要更多的实验数据。 观点总结： 1. 高超音速气流涉及气体和热防护系统材料在极端条件下的相互作用。 2. 在高超音速气流中，内能弛豫、气相反应和气体-表面相互作用的速率通常与气体运动速率相似，从而导致热化学状态失去平衡。 3. 这些速率过程会影响空气动力表现、传热速率、导致边界层转捩的不稳定性增长、催化气体-表面相互作用和烧蚀。 4. 高超音速气流对化学速率过程的缩放很敏感，解离受二元缩放控制，重组受三元缩放控制。 5. 先进的多物理场模拟和计算化学方法正被用于理解和精确模拟关键速率过程。 未来工作： 1. 验证高超音速流动模拟和基本模型仍然是一个关键问题。 在地面风洞中很难再现所有相关的速率过程，在这些气流中进行非侵入式测量也是一个挑战。 2. 应利用先进的模拟来设计针对模型不确定性的实验，这些实验可在现有风洞中进行。 3. 在开发石墨烧蚀有限速率模型方面已取得进展，但要表示更复杂的热防护材料与空气反应产物之间的相互作用，还需要做大量工作。 4. 人们很少致力于了解高超音速飞行极端条件下的湍流运动。 5. 高超音速流动的预测依赖于计算流体动力学方法，而这些方法是根据低速流动设计的方法改编而来的。 需要开发改进的数值方法，这些方法对网格缺陷不那么敏感，耗散水平低，但能捕捉到强烈的不连续性，并能有效地处理有许多化学物种和刚性源项的问题。 6. 高超音速流动环境的高保真模拟远未完成；高超音速飞行系统在飞行过程中会在很大的时间尺度范围内发生变化。 相关过程包括热膨胀、材料降解和形状变化、表面粗糙度变化以及流体与结构的相互作用和振动。

title: Developments of Chemical Non-Equilibrium Effects in Numerical Simulation of Aerodynamic Heating in Hypersonic Flow
abstract_orig: When the aircraft flies at hypersonic velocity, the intense compression of gas and the viscous block make the temperature rise sharply, which results in “thermal barrier” problem. The chemical non-equilibrium effect becomes one of the key issues in the research of hypersonic aerodynamics as the non-equilibrium effect in hypersonic flow has a great influence on the aerodynamic. Non-equilibrium effect and “real gas effect” are briefly introduced in this thesis. The developments chemical non-equilibrium effects in numerical simulation of aerodynamic heating were reviewed, including chemical non-equilibrium effect, “real gas effect”, chemical reaction model, the first grid spacing. The shock wave standoff distance is numerically simulated by chemical non-equilibrium flow passing a sphere and the relationship between the shock wave standoff distance with Mach number is analyzed, this law needs to be verified by subsequent tests. Finally, it is pointed out that the effect of turbulence on chemical non-equilibrium effect and the effect of radiation on numerical simulation of aerodynamic heating are worthy of attention.
notes: 高超声速飞行器：马赫数大于5的飞行器。 数值模拟经历了：边界层方程（BL）、粘性激波层方程（VSL）、抛物化方程（PNS）和全NS方程的求解过程。 气体状态方程经历了：量热完全气体模型、化学平衡流模型、化学非平衡流模型、热力学非平衡流模型。 真实气体效应：高温气体内在属性变化——高超声速飞行在激波层内产生的高温，能够引起气体分子的离解反应、电离反应、电子激发、光辐射等一系列现象，高温也改变了流场中气体分子不同能量模式间的能量传递方式和速率。 空气在一个大气压下发生振动激励、离解和点解的温度范围： 当温度大于800K时，因为气体分子的振动能被激发，比热和比热容会成为温度的函数，此时是完全气体状态。随着温度进一步升高，流动成为化学反应流，此时的化学发暗影需要以有限速率按照一定的松弛时间达到相应的平衡态。 平衡流是指从非平衡态向平衡态过渡过程中的化学反应时间和能力模式的振动松弛时间与流体质点流过流场的特征时间相比很小的流动，此时气体的比热是温度和压强的函数；非平衡流是指振动松弛时间和化学反应时间与流体质点流过流场的特征时间是可比拟的流动状态，处于同一量级，此时的NS方程需要与化学反应动力学方程进行耦合求解，各组分之间以有限速率进行着化学反应，需要同时考虑扩散及组分生成项对组分守恒方程的影响。 非平衡效应对飞行器的影响：（1）飞行器附近的温度和气体性质会被改变，影响气动热。（2）激波位置、形状和边界层分离区大小会被改变，影响气动力。（3）电离产生的电子会在飞行器周围形成等离子层和电子吸收无线电波，导致飞行器通讯中断。 非平衡流动的首要任务是确定化学反应速率常数，一般用Arrhenius公式计算速率。 非平衡效应相比于平衡态主要影响气动热，也即影响温度、密度，而对压强、速度影响不大。非平衡效应会使得激波后的温度高于平衡流，但因为会发生离解反应（吸热），因此温度又会快速下降。 对于考虑非平衡效应的高超声速模拟，一般会用5组分、7组分和11组分假设。当不考虑电离时，可使用5组分假设；当需要考虑电离时可使用7组分假设；当温度更高或需要考虑气体辐射时，可使用11组分假设。如下图，前6个反应式可用于5组分模型，前7个可用于7组分模型，考虑所有反应可用于11组分模型。 对于高超声速的第一层网格尺寸，不存在第一层网格高度的最优值，随着第一层网格的雷诺数减小，热流会增加到一个定值。 对于高超声速流动的数值模拟，激波脱体距离是常用于验证结果准确性的参数，而这个值与激波层内气体的热化学状态密切相关，因为脱体距离与驻点线上的平均密度成反比，故激波脱体距离可以在一定程度上反映化学反应的激烈程度。 在化学非平衡流动中，当大气层高度、钝体半径和来流密度相同时，激波脱体距离遵循随着马赫数的增加先减小后增大的变化规律，会存在一个拐点马赫数。由于非平衡效应会使化学反应以有限速率进行，气体经过激波后的碰撞次数减少，气流需要经过一段距离才到平衡态，因此非平衡流的拐点马赫数会大于平衡流。随着大气高度的增加气体密度降低，气体分子之间的碰撞减少，非平衡效应会更明显，达到平衡态需要的时间会更多。脱体激波距离的变化会影响到飞行器的整体设计。 结论：1）考虑真实气体效应后，激波层内温度降低，密度增大，而速度和压强与量热完全气体区别不大。2）化学非平衡激波后的温度高于化学平衡流，且随着气体向近壁面流动，温度逐渐下降，密度逐渐增大，呈现一个明显的非平衡变化过程，而压强和速度与化学平衡流的区别不大。3）对于化学反应模型的选取应依照实际研究。4）第一层网格高度对避免热流结果影响巨大，应尽可能小。5）化学平衡下的与化学非平衡下的激波脱体距离均随着马赫数的增加先减小后增大，存在拐点，但需实验验证。（6）化学非平衡下的最小激波脱体距离出现的马赫数比平衡态大，说明非平衡条件下气体的可压缩性增加。

title: SU2-NEMO: An Open-Source Framework for High-Mach Nonequilibrium Multi-Species Flows
abstract_orig: SU2-NEMO, a recent extension of the open-source SU2 multiphysics suite’s set of physical models and code architecture, is presented with the aim of introducing its enhanced capabilities in addressing high-enthalpy and high-Mach number ﬂows. This paper discusses the thermal nonequilibrium and ﬁnite-rate chemistry models adopted, including a link to the Mutation++ physio-chemical library. Further, the paper discusses how the software architecture has been designed to ensure modularity, incorporating the ability to introduce additional models in an efﬁcient manner. title: On unsteady boundary-layer separation in supersonic flow. Part 1. Upstream moving separation point
abstract_orig: This study is concerned with the boundary-layer separation from a rigid body surface in unsteady two-dimensional laminar supersonic ﬂow. The separation is assumed to be provoked by a shock wave impinging upon the boundary layer at a point that moves with speed Vsh along the body surface. The strength of the shock and its speed Vsh are allowed to vary with time t, but not too fast, namely, we assume that the characteristic time scale t Re−1/2/V 2 w. Here Re denotes the Reynolds number, and Vw = −Vsh is wall velocity referred to the gas velocity V∞ in the free stream. We show that under this assumption the ﬂow in the region of interaction between the shock and boundary layer may be treated as quasi-steady if it is considered in the coordinate frame moving with the shock. We start with the ﬂow regime when Vw = O(Re−1/8). In this case, the interaction between the shock and boundary layer is described by classical triple-deck theory. The main modiﬁcation to the usual triple-deck formulation is that in the moving frame the body surface is no longer stationary; it moves with the speed Vw = −Vsh. The corresponding solutions of the triple-deck equations have been constructed numerically. For this purpose, we use a numerical technique based on ﬁnite diﬀerencing along the streamwise direction and Chebyshev collocation in the direction normal to the body surface. In the second part of the paper, we assume that 1 Vw O(Re−1/8), and concentrate our attention on the self-induced separation of the boundary layer. Assuming, as before, that the Reynolds number, Re, is large, the method of matched asymptotic expansions is used to construct the corresponding solutions of the Navier–Stokes equations in a vicinity of the separation point.

title: Numerical solution of unsteady boundary-layer separation in supersonic flow: upstream moving wall
author_display: R. Yapalparvi and L. L. Van Dommelen
abstract_orig: This paper is an extension of work on separation from a downstream moving wall by Ruban et al. (J. Fluid. Mech., vol. 678, 2011, pp. 124–155) and is in particular concerned with the boundary-layer separation in unsteady two-dimensional laminar supersonic ﬂow. In a frame attached to the wall, the separation is assumed to be provoked by a shock wave impinging upon the boundary layer at a point that moves downstream with a non-dimensional speed which is assumed to be of order Re−1/8 where Re is the Reynolds number. In the coordinate system of the shock however, the wall moves upstream. The strength of the shock and its speed are allowed to vary with time on a characteristic time scale that is large compared to Re−1/4. The ‘triple-deck’ model is used to describe the interaction process. The governing equations of the interaction problem can be derived from the Navier–Stokes equations in the limit Re → ∞. The numerical solutions are obtained using a combination of ﬁnite differences along the streamwise direction and Chebyshev collocation along the normal direction in conjunction with Newton linearization. In the present study with the wall moving upstream, the evidence is inconclusive regarding the so-called ‘Moore–Rott–Sears’ criterion being satisﬁed. Instead it is observed that the pressure rise from its initial value is very slow and that a recirculation region forms, the upstream part of which is wedge-shaped, as also observed in turbulent marginal separation for large values of angle of attack.

title: Singularity in the boundary layer on an upstream-sliding wall
abstract_orig: This paper is concerned with the boundary layer on the leading edge of an aerofoil with the aerofoil surface sliding parallel to itself in the upstream direction. The flow analysis is conducted in the framework of the classical Prandtl formulation with the pressure distribution given by the solution for the outer inviscid flow. Since a reverse flow region is always present near the wall, a numerical method, where the derivatives were approximated by the windward finite differences, was used to solve the boundary-layer equations. We were interested in the flow behaviour on the upper surface of the aerofoil, but to calculate the boundary-layer equations, we had to extend the computational domain from the upper surface of the aerofoil to the lower surface. The calculations were performed for a range of angles of attack, and it is found that there exists a critical value of the angle of attack for which the Moore–Rott–Sears singularity forms in the flow. This is accompanied by an abrupt thickening of the boundary layer at the singular point and the formation of a recirculation region with closed streamlines behind this point. We further found that the flow immediately behind the singular point and in the recirculation region could be treated as inviscid, which allowed us to use the Prandtl–Batchelor theorem for theoretical modelling of the flow. A similar formulation was used earlier by Bezrodnykh et al. (Comput. Maths Math. Phys. vol. 63, 2023, pp. 2359–2371). These authors considered the boundary-layer flow on a flat plate with the pressure gradient created by a dipole situated some distance from the plate. They also found that there exists a critical value of the dipole strength for which a singularity forms in the boundary layer. However, their interpretation of the flow behaviour differs significantly from what we observe in our study.

title: Concerning marginal singularities in the boundary-layer flow on a downstream-moving surface
abstract_orig: The formation of separation singularities in solutions of the classical boundary-layer equations is studied numerically and analytically for the case of a two-dimensional incompressible steady flow near a solid surface moving in the direction of the main stream. Unlike the previously studied regime of the incipient separation located at the maximum point in the external pressure distribution, the breakdown in this work occurs under an adverse pressure forcing and involves a regular flow field upstream of the Moore-Rott-Sears point with an algebraic non-analyticity downstream. Small deviations from the precisely regular approach to the singular point are shown to result in an exponential amplification of linear disturbances; in the subsequent nonlinear stage the solution terminates in a finite-distance blow-up singularity or, alternatively, continues in a regular fashion across the singular station. The case of asymptotically small slip velocities is considered and a connection with marginal separation on a fixed wall is discussed.

title: Exact solution for heat transfer across the Sakiadis boundary layer
abstract_orig: We consider the problem of convective heat transfer across the laminar boundary layer induced by an isothermal moving surface in a Newtonian fluid. In a previous work [Barlow et al., “Exact and explicit analytical solution for the Sakiadis boundary layer,” Phys. Fluids 36, 031703 (2024)], an exact power series solution was provided for the hydrodynamic flow, often referred to as the Sakiadis boundary layer. Here, we utilize this expression to develop an exact solution for the associated thermal boundary layer as characterized by the Prandtl number (Pr) and local Reynolds number along the surface. To extract the location-dependent heat transfer coefficient (expressed in dimensionless form as the Nusselt number), the dimensionless temperature gradient at the wall is required; this gradient is solely a function of Pr and is expressed as an integral of the exact boundary layer flow solution. We find that the exact solution for the temperature gradient is computationally unstable at large Pr, and a large Pr expansion for the temperature gradient is obtained using Laplace's method. A composite solution is obtained, which is accurate to O(10−10). Although divergent, the classical power series solution for the Sakiadis boundary layer—expanded about the wall—may be used to obtain all higher-order corrections in the asymptotic expansion. We show that this result is connected to the physics of large Prandtl number flows where the thickness of the hydrodynamic boundary layer is much larger than that of the thermal boundary layer. The present model is valid for all Prandtl numbers and attractive for ease of use.

title: A study of the flow structure for Mach reflection in steady supersonic flow
author_display: B. Gao and Z. N. Wu
abstract_orig: In this paper we study the waves generated over the slipline and their interactions with other waves for Mach reflection in steady two-dimensional supersonic flow. We find that a series of expansion and compression waves exist over the slip line, even in the region immediately behind the leading part of the reflected shock wave, previously regarded as a uniform flow. These waves make the leading part of the slipline, previously regarded as straight, deviate nonlinearly towards the reflecting surface. When the transmitted expansion waves from the upper corner first intersect the slipline, an inflexion point is produced. Downstream of this inflexion point, compression waves are produced over the slipline. By considering the interaction between the various expansion or compression waves, we obtain a Mach stem height, the shape and position of the slipline and reflected shock wave, compared well to computational fluid dynamics (CFD) results. We also briefly consider the case with a subsonic portion behind the reflected shock wave. The global flow pattern is obtained through CFD and the starting point of the sonic line is identified through a simple analysis. The sonic line appears to coincide with the first Mach wave from the upper corner expansion fan after transmitted from the reflected shock wave.

title: Shock reflection with the influence of wave structures near the intersection point in confined-space double-wedge
abstract_orig: To understand the reflection type of incident shock wave under the influence of the wave structures near the intersection point of shock/shock interaction in confined-space double-wedge. The evolution of the flow field and shock reflection is comprehensively analyzed for various relative positions of the incident shock wave and expansion waves, which controlled by contraction ratio (Cr) of the double-wedge. Computational results show that expansion wave of Type VI has limited impact on the reflection type of oblique shock wave above detachment condition. When the expansion waves cover the incident shock wave, The critical Cr for the RR-MR transition on the opposite wall is determined when expansion waves fully cover the incident shock, and a subsonic region following RR is observed. Additional insight into the trend of Mach stem height along increasing Cr shows linear or nonlinear mode, which is dominated by the related position of expansion fans. It is also shown that the shock wave near the intersection point of Type I contributes subtle effect on the reflection type at the opposite wall.

title: Regular reflection to Mach reflection (RR–MR) transition in short wedges
author_display: Vinod Yeldho Baby, Vinoth Paramanantham and G. Rajesh
abstract_orig: Regular reﬂection (RR) to Mach reﬂection (MR) transitions (RR ↔ MR) on long wedges in steady supersonic ﬂows have been well studied and documented. However, in a short wedge where the wedge length is small, the transition prediction becomes really challenging owing to the interaction of the expansion fan emanating from the trailing edge of the wedge with the incident shock and the triple/reﬂection point. The extent of this interaction depends on the distance between the wedge trailing edge and the symmetry line (Ht). This distance is a geometric combination of the distance of the wedge leading edge from the symmetry line (H), the wedge angle (θ) and the wedge length (w). In the present study, we used the method of characteristics to model the complete wave interactions which accurately predicted shock curvatures and the reﬂection conﬁgurations for all ranges of the incoming ﬂow Mach number. In the case of short wedges, the transition criterion strongly depends on the wedge length, which can be so adjusted even to eliminate the RR → MR transitions till the wedge angle reaches the no-reﬂection domain. Transition lines for both the detachment criterion and von Neumann criterion are also drawn to investigate the dual solution domain, and the reﬂection conﬁgurations were veriﬁed experimentally for the ﬁrst time on short wedges. By using proper input conﬁguration parameter (w/H), various types of shifts in the dual solution domain for short wedges are studied and categorised into three types, namely Type I, Type II and Type III.

title: Mach reflection promoted by an upstream shock wave
abstract_orig: , Mach reflection subjected to the influence of an upstream shock wave from the same side is studied here. This situation occurs when two incident shock waves induced by a double wedge reflect at the same point of the reflecting surface and when the downstream incident shock wave is stronger than the upstream one. A shock polar analysis is used to show that this configuration produces an inverted Mach stem and a type IV shock interference between the Mach stem and the upstream shock wave. This shock interference produces a jet that divides the flow stream downstream of the Mach stem into two ducts with different sonic throats, thus complicating the mechanism by which the Mach stem size is determined. A transition analysis shows that the Mach reflection of the downstream shock wave is promoted by the upstream one. Computational fluid dynamics is used to assess the flow pattern anticipated by shock polar analysis and demonstrates how the heights of Mach stem and jet depend on the inflow Mach number and wedge turning angle.

title: Transition of shock reflection with downstream expansion fan interference
abstract_orig: In this paper, the reﬂection of shock waves with downstream expansion fan interference in two-dimensional, inviscid ﬂow is investigated, including steady Mach reﬂection (MR) and the unsteady transition process from regular reﬂection (RR) to MR. A threshold for the conﬁguration based on non-dimensional wedge length is proposed. The analytical model for the steady MR and RR→MR transition process is established based on the classical shock and expansion wave relations, whose prediction agrees well with results obtained through inviscid numerical simulation. It is found that the expansion fan interference signiﬁcantly inﬂuences the steady ﬂow patterns, especially the height of the Mach stem and the shape of the slip line. The interaction accelerates the formation of the sonic throat, stabilizing the ﬂow structure rapidly, and results in generally small Mach stem heights. The exposure of the triple point to the expansion fan eliminates the inﬂection point on the slip line, whose slope increases smoothly. The interaction further affects the time evolution of the Mach stem during the multiple-interaction stage of the RR→MR transition process. It appears that the modiﬁcations come from the curvature of the incident shock brought by the wave interference. During the multiple-interaction stage, the triple point moves upstream along the curved incident shock, where the incident shock angle changes according to the curvature, resulting in the variation of the evolution velocity.
